actions.reason:
No change cleared the 1.0% minimum on decode_ir in four evaluations, so I am not submitting anything. Every build kept outputs byte-identical to the parent. Ratios by evaluation (decode / check / encode):
1. Try-and-subscript lookups for the decode plan, merge plan and encode table, with merge plans keyed by digit count: 0.9937 / 0.9963 / 0.9991.
2. Plus b58decode_int calling b58decode instead of keeping its own copy of the lane-merge code: 0.9913 / 0.9925 / 0.9960.
3. Plus folding _get_base58_decode_map into _get_base58_decode_table and dropping the unused wrapper.cache attribute: 0.9902 / 0.9914 / 0.9950. This came closest, just short of the required 0.9900.
4. Plus removing the itertools.product import and the redundant memoiser on the merge builder: decode jumped back to 0.9986 (check 0.9922, encode 0.9950).
I don't know why the fourth step made decode worse. The two candidate causes are the import removal and the merge builder losing its cache; this run doesn't show which. A follow-up could start from the third version and try more per-call savings in b58decode, leaving out the fourth step's edits.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I worked on decode in base58-py. Same bytes out was the bar. First I swapped the plan and table lookups to try-and-subscript, with merge plans keyed by digit count. Then I had b58decode_int call b58decode, and trimmed more code in later rounds.

Four evaluations, four rejections. Every build gave identical outputs. Decode ratios ran 0.9937, 0.9913, 0.9902, then 0.9986. The bar was 0.9900. Evaluation 5 missed it by a hair, with check at 0.9914 and encode at 0.9950. The last round slid back. I submitted nothing.

What I believe now: the lookup overhead is real but small. Trimming it gives under 1% on decode_ir. The cost sits in the big-int arithmetic, not the dictionary access. More shaving here is a long ebb with little water in it. Not measured yet: where decode actually spends its steps.

Next I will profile b58decode by step count per input size before editing anything.
